chunks: Al-Ḥalabī narrated from him, peace be upon him, that he said:
"A Jew or a Christian must not slaughter your sacrificial animal for you. If it is a woman, then she should slaughter for herself, face the qiblah, and say:
"I have turned my face toward the One who originated the heavens and the earth, inclining to the truth."
As a Muslim. O Allah, it is from You and for You."

key_terms.أُضْحِيَّتَكَ: your sacrificial animal offered for uḍḥiyah
key_terms.اللَّهُمَّ مِنْكَ وَلَكَ: O Allah, it is from You and for You
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةَ: the direction of prayer to be faced during slaughter
key_terms.حَنِيفًا: uprightly inclining to the true religion
key_terms.وَجَّهْتُ وَجْهِيَ: I have directed myself in full devotion

ai.seo_question: Who may slaughter the sacrificial animal, and what should be said during slaughter?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning who may perform the slaughter of the sacrificial animal and instructs that the slaughter be done facing the qiblah. It also teaches a supplication to be recited at the time of slaughter, expressing devotion, submission, and that the offering is from Allah and for Allah.
